new_text: Those two directions therefore do not explain the difference, and its cause is not established here. The dose does not explain the difference. Two dose definitions are both right: the mean of per-position ratios of the ban-free unit to the ban unit is 0.99, 0.89, 0.99, 0.87 and 1.39 on connected components, shortest path, two sum, grid and kth smallest, and the ratio of mean norms over blocks 12 to 23 is 0.75, 0.84, 0.78, 0.75 and 0.97 (Table 174); the ratio of mean norms equals the ban-norm-weighted mean of the per-block ratios exactly (residual below 1e-6), and the gap between the definitions sits within blocks (per-position ratios against ratios of block means, which also mixes the bf16 engine's own ban unit), not in the weighting across blocks. At the bf16 dose expressed in 8-bit ban units, the 8-bit dose-response curve (correct off-default share, alpha 0 to 4) predicts more escapes than bf16 produced on connected components at alpha 2 (exact binomial p 2.9e-18 under both definitions), shortest path at alpha 1 and 2 (p 0.00051 and 4.7e-05; 0.015 at the lower Clopper-Pearson bound) and kth smallest (alpha 1, p 0.00081), and not on grid or two sum. With correct-only shares on both engines the alpha-2 drop is 20-fold on connected components, 6-fold on shortest path, 3-fold on grid and 1.6-fold on kth smallest (Fisher p 7.2e-11 and 0.00091 on the first two), against a dose shortfall of at most 13% (mean of ratios) or 25% (ratio of means). The cause is not established: engine, GPU, kernel and sampler streams all differ between the two runs, and Claim E decides it. [iteration-6 correction]

new_text:
5. *The record repairs.* The held-out movability test is inconclusive under catalogue-only avoidance and disconfirmed under the drop sensitivity; the read position and condition sentence are inert only at per-position doses up to 4 ban units; landing comparisons on matched events give push -0.76 against association -3.11 on 3 events and -1.37 against -3.46 on 5.

**Descriptive leads.** [iteration-6 correction]

1. *Where a random nudge moves the instruct model, it often lands on the base model's runner-up, but the tuned twin had often written that landing already.* Over the 21 iteration-5 landing events the base runner-up named the modal landing 17 times (new Qwen3-8B units 6 of 7, Poisson-binomial p 0.0027; Gemma 5 of 7, p 0.025; 8-bit screen 5 of 5; bf16 remeasure 1 of 2; 15 of 19 unit clusters). 6 of the hits are landings the twin had already written among its 50 programs, and the twin's own most frequent correct non-default program names the landing on 6 of the 7 events where it exists, with no event on which the two forecasts disagree (0 discordant pairs). On the events whose twin wrote no correct non-default program, the base runner-up hits 3 of 4 in Qwen3-8B (p 0.052) and 2 of 4 in Gemma (p 0.42), 5 of 8 pooled (p 0.053), short of 0.05. Gemma's forecasts rest on thin support: its grid runner-up comes from 4 valid attempts and 0 correct programs, kth smallest's and connected components' from 6 and 6 valid attempts, and its base labels agree with adjudication at 0.64. The base composition is ahead of association by 0.75 nats on new tasks (exact Wilcoxon p 0.055) and 1.50 in Gemma (p 0.023; 1.57 over the 6 events where association is defined).
